actions.title: Navigate the app to a route
Clear a per-account feature-flag override (revert to inherit)
actions.description: Remove a feature flag's PER-ACCOUNT override for one account, so the account reverts to inheriting the global default (or the compiled default).

account_id.description: The account UUID whose override should be cleared.

actions.title: Enable or disable a feature flag for one account (per-account override)
actions.description: Set a PER-ACCOUNT override for a feature flag (on/off) for a single account, leaving the global default and other accounts untouched.

account_id.description: The account UUID to override the flag for.

enabled.description: true enables the feature for this account, false disables it.

actions.title: Enable or disable a feature flag (global default)
actions.description: Set a feature flag's GLOBAL default on or off for the whole deployment (no per-account override).

enabled.description: true enables the feature globally, false disables it.

actions.title: Go back to the previous step
actions.description: On a step of a new analysis, go back to the step this path showed before, or to where the path started. Refused while a run is starting or a dialog is open.

actions.title: Set the last draw you will use
actions.description: On the questions step of a new analysis, set "Last draw you will use": the day, counted from the start of treatment, of the last blood draw the analysis uses. It is also the decision day. A whole day from 1; the files are checked again for the new day.

day.description: The day of the last draw, counted from the start of treatment.

actions.title: Start a new analysis
actions.description: Pick one of the two ways of the Start screen: "train" learns from your own patients, "predict" predicts new patients with a ready-made model, a saved model or an opened model file. The old two-list spellings stay accepted: "pretrained" (a ready-made model from the lab) and "reuse" (a model you saved) both start the predict way with that list pinned. Opens the first step of that way, its file step (the learn way asks its questions after the files); files already added are kept. Back from that step returns to the page it was started from. Refused while a run is starting or a dialog is open.

intent.description: "predict" (any model), "train" (learn from my data), or the old list spellings "pretrained" (a ready-made model) / "reuse" (a saved model).

startAtFiles.description: Open the file step directly (every path already starts with its file step; kept for older callers).

actions.title: Use the example data in a flow
actions.description: The one-click example path of the Start cards (and Help's try-it cards): "predict" adopts the example patients-to-predict table, ensures the "Example models" set (usually under a minute; the first time also downloads the methods) and opens the predict path's file step with that set ticked once it checks out; "train" fills the learn path's study answers and both example files and opens its file step. Back from the step returns to the page it was started from. Refused while a run is starting or a dialog is open.

intent.description: "predict" (the example patients to predict + the example models) or "train" (learn from my data).

actions.title: Go back from Help to the step it was opened from
actions.description: On Help opened from a step of a new analysis (a problem code link on the file step, for example), go back to that step. The step keeps what was entered there. Offered only then.

actions.title: Use the settings of a past analysis again
actions.description: History "Use these settings again": copy the settings of a past analysis (by its run id) into the method choice and open it. The files of that analysis are not reused. Back from the method choice returns to the page it was started from.

runId.description: The run id of the past analysis (from History).

actions.title: Set how the methods pick their markers
actions.description: Set how the methods that pick their markers from your file choose them (the study step's group): 'ranked' uses the markers that best separate the outcome (the default), 'chosen' uses the marker you name first (the others follow the ranking), 'leave_out' leaves those methods out. A chosen marker must be one of your file's main markers; a marker the file does not have is refused.

mode.description: ranked (the default), chosen (with marker), or leave_out.

marker.description: The file marker to use first (required with mode: chosen).

actions.title: Set the study answers
actions.description: Set the answers of the questions step of a new analysis: the disease, the treatments and what to predict. They are the method filters — an answered disease or treatment tick excludes methods not made for it. An id the method list does not know is refused. Omit a field to leave it as it is; send null (or an empty list) to clear it.

disease_group.description: A disease id of the method list (a category, a disease or a sub-group), or null to clear it.

treatment_classes.description: The ticked treatment-class ids of the method list (an empty list clears the tick).

outcome.description: The outcome pill: binary-response, response-probability, progression-by-day or dynamic-risk; null clears it.

actions.title: Update MCP settings
actions.description: Update the MCP agent/tool caps (max concurrent control sessions, max in-flight invokes per user, per-action wall-clock backstop, list-capabilities cap, invoke result-byte cap) and the pairing-code TTL. Each field is optional; omit to leave unchanged. Values are bounded (safety limits).

max_control_sessions.description: Global cap on live agent control sessions — an OOM safety limit (16..16384).

max_inflight_per_user.description: Per-user cap on concurrent in-flight invokes — a DoS safety limit (1..256).

action_wall_clock_secs.description: Outer wall-clock backstop on one dispatched action, in seconds (30..3600).

max_list_results.description: Cap on capabilities returned by one list_capabilities call (1..2000).

max_result_bytes.description: Cap on the invoke result body relayed to the model, in bytes — an OOM safety limit (1 KiB..64 MiB).

actions.title: Check for method updates
actions.description: Ask the app to check now for a newer signed method list. A verified newer list is used from the next run on (a run already going keeps its list); the answer is the list in use and what the check found (current, updated, unreachable, refused, …).

actions.title: Choose a method preset
actions.description: On the choose-methods page, select the methods of one preset: recommended, all that can run, fast only (under 1 min each), or none. It replaces the current selection. Refused until the method list has loaded.

preset.description: Preset: recommended, all, fast or none

actions.title: Tick or untick methods
actions.description: On the choose-methods page, tick or untick the named methods (one key per click; the Extra-inputs switch's automatic untick passes all of them at once). Refused until the method list has loaded, and refused for a method that cannot run with these files.

keys.description: The method keys to tick or untick.

actions.title: Delete a model set
actions.description: Open the delete confirmation for a set of saved models (by its id). The set is NOT deleted by this action: the confirmation dialog opens and the person confirms there (the files go with the models, the results already made are kept).

setId.description: The set id (from the model sets list).

actions.title: Export a model set
actions.description: Download a set of saved models (by its id) as the .txr set file: the browser download on the website, the Save dialog in the desktop app. Refused when the set is not in the current model sets list.

setId.description: The set id (from the model sets list).

actions.title: Open a model file
actions.description: Open a saved model container (.txr file): on the Start page the picker opens in place and the imported model lands on the Models page; with no open picker (the agent path) it opens the Models page instead, where "Open a model file" is the same affordance. Refused in demo mode.

actions.title: Rename a model set
actions.description: Rename a set of saved models (by its id, the name the "Your models" page shows for the set). The set and its model rows keep every other fact; the new name is shown everywhere the set is named.

setId.description: The set id (from the model sets list).

actions.title: Run the chosen models
actions.description: On the model step (the merged model list), start the run with the models that are checked. Refused when the chosen models were trained at different decision days (each model runs at its own day), when no model is chosen, and when a selected lab model cannot be run (a download still running or failed). Requires the current state token (view.describe).

expected.description: The current state token of the model list (view.describe._state_token).

actions.title: Filter and sort the model list
actions.description: On the merged model list, set the view: the source chips (From the lab / Saved / Imported), "Can run only", the host chips (Same outcome as my file, Published rules, Learned by the benchmark, Checked on 2 or more other cohorts), the search text over the run name and the sort. Each omitted field keeps the current value; "all" is cleared by passing empty sources, no chips and canRunOnly false. Requires the current state token (view.describe).

expected.description: The current state token of the model list (view.describe._state_token).

sources.description: The source chips to show ("lab", "saved", "imported"; several on = any of them).

canRunOnly.description: Show only the models that can run on the file.

chips.description: The other host chips to show.

search.description: Text to find over the run name and the model facts.

actions.title: Select models to run
actions.description: On the merged model list, set the checked models by their row ids (the same write the checkboxes and "Select all that can run" make). Rows the list shows as cannot run are never selectable. Requires the current state token (view.describe).

expected.description: The current state token of the model list (view.describe._state_token).

ids.description: The row ids to check (the selection replaces the current one).

actions.title: Switch between the ready-made models and your saved models
actions.description: On the model step of a new analysis, show the other model kind of the one merged list: "saved" turns the Saved and Imported chips on, "published" turns the From the lab chip on. Everything else (the searched file, the selection) stays; the old two-list switch is this alias's mapping.

list.description: "saved" for your saved models, "published" for the ready-made models.

actions.title: Predict new patients with a saved model
actions.description: Your models "Use": start the predict path for one saved model (by its id). Opens the step to add the patients to predict; the model is ticked on the merged model list once the file checks out. Back from that step returns to the page it was started from.

modelId.description: The saved model id (from Your models).

name.description: The model name the step shows.

actions.title: Go to AI Assistant Access settings
Turn the extra inputs on or off
actions.description: On the choose-methods step, turn the Extra-inputs switch on or off. The switch decides whether the run uses the file's extra-input columns; a method that REQUIRES them is still tickable with the switch off. Turning it off by hand while a required method is ticked unticks that method (it needs extra inputs) and keeps the switch off.

on.description: Turn the switch on or off.

actions.title: Set the decision day or the look-ahead day
actions.description: On the choose-methods step, set the decision day or the look-ahead day (the day the prediction is for), both counted from the start of treatment. The look-ahead day must be after the decision day and within the limit; a day where no patient has a known outcome is refused. With a ready-made or saved model the look-ahead is the model's own and cannot be set.

day.description: The day, counted from the start of treatment.

actions.title: Set up WSL
actions.description: Windows only: start installing WSL 2, which methods run in, or updating it when it is too old (Microsoft's own `wsl --install --no-distribution`, after `wsl --update` for an old WSL), run as administrator. Answers at once with the setup's status (running: true); nothing runs until the person at the PC confirms in TxResBench's own dialog (an agent cannot answer it); Windows may also ask for permission. Read how it went with Sandbox.listEnvs (GET /api/sandbox/envs): once stack.wsl_setup.running is false, stack.wsl_setup.last says done (start the app again, after restarting Windows when restart_windows), declined (not offered again for a minute: retry_in_secs), not_started (Windows' error) or failed (wsl.exe's exit code and last lines). Offered only while the app found WSL missing or too old and no setup runs.

actions.title: Get the current selection, if any (best-effort)
Describe a live view instance (its current state + state token)
List every live, AI-drivable view instance
